newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TELKOM TO GET $1BLN OF PRIVATISATION CASH.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TELKOM TO GET $1BLN OF PRIVATISATION CASH.

text.p: South Africa's Telkom will receive $1 billion of the proceeds from the sale of a 30 percent stake in the telecommunications concern with the balance going to the state, deputy president Thabo Mbeki said on Tuesday.

"I am happy to announce to the people of South Africa that government has decided on the injection of $1 billion of the proceeds of the sale into Telkom to help fund the infrastructure expansion programme," Mbeki told a telecommunications conference.
"The rest of the proceeds will go to the National Revenue Fund.
"This will commit Telkom to one of the most aggressive roll-out programmes of its kind in the world," he said.

Mbeki said the government had given its approval for the immediate finalisation of the sale of the 30 percent stake in state-run Telkom to a consortium comprising SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd .

Telkom chairman Dikgang Moseneke said the sale would be settled by a one-off payment in dollars. Officials said the money would be paid at the close of the deal which could be one week to 90 days from the signing, now expected within the next few days.

Mbeki said Telkom and its partners estimated that 50,000 jobs would be created in the telcommunications sector alone from the increased capital expenditure of Telkom which will almost double in the next five years.
"The boost to the economy will be enormous," he said.
